One question still open for the client (not a build defect). V1's rating ladder is not monotonically descending: Fetch 8.4 sits at rank 2, above Embrace 8.5 at rank 3 — so a lower-scored partner outranks a higher-scored one on screen. This matches the supplied sheet exactly, so it is built correctly; flagging it only in case the sheet itself was an oversight. V2–V6 use a position-locked ladder and have no such inversion.

The brief being tested against

Six variations, each testing a different partner in the #1 spot. Apply the test ranking for the All Pets, Cats and Dogs filters; revert to the hardcoded ranking when Breeds or Enter Zip is selected. The client confirmed they accept a partner's rating changing when a breed is picked (ratings revert along with order — a deliberate change from the previous SWF164, where ratings persisted under every filter). The "Show More" button must sit after Trupanion in all variations; its position does not change per variation.

Trupanion sits at position 6 in every one of the six variations, so the collapsed state must show exactly 6 cards, ending on Trupanion.

BUG-01 — V4/V5/V6 never collapsed, "Show More" was invisible FIXED & VERIFIED 2026-09-23

Resolved. V4, V5 and V6 now load with exactly 6 cards ending on Trupanion, and the injected .cre-t-164-toggle computes to display: flex and is clickable, expanding to 10 and collapsing back. Verified on Chrome Desktop, Mobile Chrome, Firefox and WebKit. V1/V2/V3 show no regression.

Before → after

Root cause, as diagnosed on 2026-09-22 (kept for the record)

Symptom. V4, V5 and V6 loaded showing all 10 cards instead of 6. The .cre-t-164-toggle element was injected into the DOM with the correct "Show More" label, but computed to display: none, so a user could never click it. The native toggle was hidden too, so the entire Show More / Show Less feature was absent.

Cause — the CSS files had split into two groups. All six JS files were functionally identical (diff showed only whitespace and comments outside the partnerRatingData array), and all six correctly added .cre-t-164-below-trupanion to ranks 7–10 and toggled body.cre-t-164-collapsed. But the JS relied on CSS to do the actual hiding, and the CSS differed:

RuleV1 / V3 stylesheetsV4 / V5 / V6 stylesheets
Hide ranks 7–10 while collapsedpresentMISSING
Show the injected togglepositive rule — display: flex !importantreplaced by a negative rule that never turned it on

Why it shipped: the header comment in the V4/V5/V6 stylesheets asserted the CSS was "identical across V1-V6" and that "Show More is entirely native's own DOM mount/unmount — we never manage visibility of the 10 slots ourselves. No defensive 'force visible' rule needed." Both statements were false: the JS hid the native toggle and injected its own clone, so with no positive rule nothing was ever shown or hidden. Hashing the stylesheets (after normalising CRLF) gave two distinct values, not one — the lesson being to diff per-variation files against each other, not just against the spec.

Filter behaviour — verified live

Gating is driven by shouldRevert(), which returns true only when a breed or a ZIP is present — pet type is deliberately excluded, exactly as the brief requires.

The previous SWF164's collapse-fighting bug is fixed and stays fixed. The old build ran a 250 ms interval that unconditionally re-added the collapsed class, so clicking "Show More" within ~3 s of load was silently undone, and the collapse re-fired on every return to All Pets. That failure mode once survived a full rewrite on this site, so it was re-probed deliberately in both rounds of testing: runCycle() no longer re-adds the class — it is set once in init() and on a genuine filter-context change. Clicking "Show More" 0.9 s after the list appears still shows 10 cards five seconds later, and returning to All Pets no longer re-collapses.
Method note. Breed was exercised via the ?breed= URL parameter. The site's real MUI #breed-select combobox stays Mui-disabled under synthetic input, so the parameter is the reliable proxy for "a breed is selected" — one manual pass on the real widget is still worth doing before launch.

Every ordering and every rating matches the supplied sheet. Rank numbers renumber 1–10 correctly in all six. The Best Overall duplicate card syncs to the new #1 in all six — verified visually on V4, which shows Pumpkin at 9.6 with Pumpkin's own copy rather than Lemonade's app-store blurb. The competing cre-t-135 rating widget is hidden under cre-t-164-default, so no double rating is ever shown.

V1's rating ladder is not monotonically descending — Fetch 8.4 at rank 2 sits above Embrace 8.5 at rank 3. It matches the sheet, so it is built to spec and is not a defect; raising it only because a higher-scored partner ranked below a lower-scored one is visible to users. Needs a yes/no from the client before launch.

The Firefox and WebKit pass closes an open question from the first round: getBestOverallCard() and getPartnerCard() use :has() inside querySelector, which is a concern only on older browsers. Both engines handle it correctly. One WebKit/V4 run timed out before the site's own comparison table rendered at all — so no test code had anything to act on — and passed fully on retry against the identical URL. WebKit is the slowest engine on this site; recorded for transparency, not attributable to this test's code.

Console

Zero cre-t-164-related console errors in any variation, on either viewport. Desktop loads show 4 baseline errors and mobile 0 — the same counts appear on the control, and they are third-party 403 resource failures unrelated to this test.

Remaining open items

  • V1's non-monotonic rating ladder (Fetch 8.4 at rank 2 above Embrace 8.5 at rank 3) — matches the sheet, built correctly, needs a client yes/no.
  • Breed tested via the ?breed= URL parameter, not the real MUI #breed-select combobox, which stays Mui-disabled under synthetic input. One manual pass on the real widget is worth doing.
  • Duplicate-init guard not tested — re-running the variation JS should not double-inject the toggle.
  • Tablet viewports not covered.
  • Internal housekeeping (not user-facing): the fix was deployed to Convert but not back-ported to the local scratch variation files, which still hold the pre-fix code — anyone retesting by local injection will reproduce a defect that no longer exists live.
